recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆母細胞，核染色質細緻，核的一側有凹陷（箭頭），凹陷處對應一塊淡染的細胞質，形成像被拇指壓過的「杯狀」核（cup-like/thumbprint），常見於NPM1突變AML。
features: Blast about 2-3 times red cell diameter with fine, open chromatin
Nuclear invagination along one margin (arrow) producing a cup-like/thumbprint indentation
Pale cytoplasmic zone filling the nuclear indentation
Moderate rim of blue-grey cytoplasm without visible Auer rods
Adjacent monocytoid cell with folded nucleus and vacuolated cytoplasm; background red cells unremarkable
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a blast with fine chromatin, a moderate rim of blue-grey cytoplasm, and a prominent nuclear invagination (arrow) filled by pale cytoplasm, giving a cup-like or thumbprint appearance. No Auer rods are seen. A monocytoid cell with a folded nucleus and a lymphocyte are also present. Cup-like blasts are a morphologic clue to AML, particularly with NPM1 and/or FLT3-ITD mutations; molecular testing is recommended.

ddx.vs: Microgranular APL cells have bilobed, butterfly-shaped nuclei with fine granules and Auer rods, and are CD34/HLA-DR negative with PML::RARA.
Promonocytes have delicately folded or convoluted nuclei with grey vacuolated cytoplasm rather than a single sharp invagination with a pale zone.

ddx.dx: Cleaved lymphoma cells or reactive lymphocyte
ddx.vs: Lymphoid cells show condensed chromatin with a narrow cleft and no pale cytoplasmic pocket, and are MPO negative.
